NEW IN 2.9
• Natural voices take far less space: most are about a quarter of the size and sound the same, and each voice keeps only one copy on the phone. Voices you already have shrink with the next voice update.
• New natural voices: a second Catalan voice (Ona, Enhanced), Emirati Arabic (female), and a second German and Italian speaker.
• Each language offers its two best-sounding voices, with better choices for Bengali, Malayalam and Nepali. Voices you already have keep working.
• Indian English Rahul is back, no longer mumbles long sentences, and reads short labels at normal speed.
• Short forms like OTP, UPI and KYC are read letter by letter, phone numbers digit by digit, and app names like PhonePe more clearly.
• Typing, deleting and moving by letter in Hindi and other Indian languages reads each letter clearly, including कि, क् and क्ष.
• Devanagari text is read by the right voice sentence by sentence, and languages that share a script, like Ukrainian and Russian, are told apart.
• Settings have a new look, with previews for voice tuning, pauses, punctuation, numbers and mixed-language reading.
• Number reading mode can read digits, pairs or groups of three with a short pause.
• The app is smaller to download and uses about 30 MB less space on the phone.
• The hardware acceleration switch is gone: it made natural voices slower. The Snapdragon version still uses the NPU.
• Test voice plays sound again, numbers are no longer skipped, and crashes and TalkBack issues are fixed.

NEW IN 2.8
• Downloading natural voices is easier: each language and each voice has its own page, voices are grouped by country with yours first, and Back goes one step at a time.
• Every natural voice now has a sample to play before you download it.
• Test voice speaks Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Nepali, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Assamese, Kazakh, Kurdish and Sinhala instead of an English sentence.
• Settings fit the screen in landscape, clear of the navigation bar.
• Rasa natural voices speak in each speaker's clearest style.
• Less hiss in the Gujarati (Hetal), Indian English (Priya) and American English (LJSpeech) natural voices, and no hiss before they start speaking.
• Indian English natural voices no longer say "phone" as "phoned" at the end of a sentence.
• The speaking style setting now works with the SYSPIN natural voices too.
• Installed SYSPIN and Rasa voices download their improved version once.
• Kannada, Tamil, Malayalam and the other Rasa voices now speak inside English and Hindi text, for example with TalkBack in English.
• Numbers a natural voice cannot say are read by eSpeak instead of being skipped.
• SYSPIN voices say a single word clearly, like "Delhi" inside Hindi text.
• A name in brackets or quotes stays with its own language, like "(Arijit Singh)" in Hindi text.
• On slower phones, mixed-language text switches voices with shorter gaps.
• On phones too slow for Standard voices, Compact versions come first, and a Standard voice can be swapped for its Compact version in one tap.
• A second Rasa voice installs at once, without downloading the shared model again.
• Fewer clicks where natural voices start and stop.

NEW IN 2.7
• 42 new natural voices from IISc SYSPIN and AI4Bharat Rasa: Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, Tamil, Malayalam, Punjabi, Assamese, Nepali and Indian English, and the first natural voices for Bhojpuri, Chhattisgarhi, Magahi, Maithili, Sanskrit, Bodo and Dogri.
• Bhojpuri, Chhattisgarhi, Magahi, Maithili, Sanskrit, Bodo and Dogri become languages of their own, for apps and screen readers, once you download a voice for them.
• Compact versions of the larger voices: about twice as fast on most phones. The download list suggests the right one for your phone.
• Phrases your screen reader repeats, like "Button" and "Double-tap to activate", start at once, even after your phone restarts speech.
• Snapdragon version: a separate download that runs natural voices on the NPU of recent Snapdragon phones, much faster. The app suggests it on phones that have one, and it installs over this app.
• Natural voices update themselves when an improved version is published.
• The new voices read numbers as words in Hindi, Tamil and Nepali.
• New community natural voices: two more Tamil voices and a British English voice.
• Natural voices start speaking sooner, most of all on long sentences and with Enhanced voices.
• Words in a language none of your natural voices speak, like Gujarati or English inside Hindi, are read by eSpeak in that language instead of by the natural voice.
• Mixed-language text: choose the language numbers and times are read in. Times like 10:30 are read as times.
• The Australian English natural voice is no longer offered: it read English words inside other languages badly. If you have it, choose another English voice, like Indian English, and delete it in Downloaded voices.

NEW IN 2.6
• Mixed-language text, a new settings page: choose the language for words in each script. Read Devanagari as Marathi or Nepali, English words in Hindi text with an Indian accent, and Russian, Hebrew, Telugu, Odia, Chinese or Japanese as words instead of letter by letter. Nothing changes until you choose.
• eSpeak voices now hand Hindi words to your Hindi natural voice too, and you can turn this switching off.
• Natural voices: choose a speaking style, give each voice its own speed, and pick the speaker of voices that hold several.
• Hindi natural voices say ड़ and ढ़ clearly, as in सड़क and पढ़ना, instead of garbling them.
• Punctuation and symbols are named in your voice's language, the way NVDA reads them: Arabic, Hindi, German, Spanish, Chinese and 55 more languages no longer hear English words like "comma".
• Phonetic letters speak your voice's language too, like NVDA: b is Berlin in German, б is Борис in Russian, and Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters come with example words.
• Natural voices pronounce many more words correctly in Nepali, Urdu, Telugu, Malayalam and Bengali, and in older Portuguese, Ukrainian, Swedish, Catalan and German voices.
• The natural voices you used last are ready as soon as speech starts, so the first sentence is not read by eSpeak.
• New community natural voices: Indian English, American English with 16 speakers, Nepali with 18, Australian English with 10, Kurdish (Kurmanji) with 90, Latvian, and a second Sinhala voice.

NEW IN 2.5.2
• Mixed-language text switches voice the way eSpeak does: Hindi inside English text is read by your Hindi natural voice. Choose a natural voice for both languages; on phones with less memory the main voice reads everything.
• Central Kurdish reads words that start with two consonants correctly, like نڤێژ, and uses the Kurdish r sounds.
• Malayalam words ending in a chillu letter and Persian words with a joiner are read correctly again.
• Combined emoji, like a family, are named as one again.
• Very long text without punctuation no longer breaks an emoji in two.
• Give feedback from About: join the adev ally group on WhatsApp.

FIXED IN 2.5.1
• The user dictionary opens again, and rules can be edited and deleted.
• Natural voices no longer crash speech, including when moving quickly through items.
• A natural voice that keeps failing on your phone switches to eSpeak instead of stopping speech.
• Natural voices are off until you turn them on, and nothing about them runs while off.
• The app no longer uses the internet at start-up; only voice downloads do.
• Download suggestions match what your phone can play without pauses.
• Dictionary export keeps every part of each rule and matches NVDA's format.
• Speech keeps working even if a setting is damaged.
• Activity logs and backups no longer include your reading history.
• Clearer error messages, and no crash on devices without a file picker.

NATURAL VOICES
• Download human-sounding voices and choose, language by language, whether eSpeak or a natural voice speaks. They follow this app's pronunciation rules and your dictionary. Turn them on in Natural voices; until then everything is plain eSpeak.
• Standard and Enhanced quality, with a suggestion for your phone.
• Community voices for Tamil and Sinhala.
• Long texts play smoothly, voices load in about a second and use little memory.
• Hindi and Urdu sentences end with a natural tone.

NEW FEATURES
• Settings search from the top bar.
• Voice profiles: save and share your variant, rate, pitch and punctuation as a file.
• Favorite voices stay at the top of the voice list.
• Sleep timer, in Locks.
• Reading history (opt-in), in Tools.
• Touch and hold a language to hear a sample.

VOICES AND LANGUAGES
• Better pronunciation for Assamese, Gujarati, Nepali, Punjabi, Konkani and Sinhala.
• Indian English sounds closer to real Indian English.
• Lakh and crore reading can be used with every voice, and Hinglish, abbreviations and money reading work with more voices.

ACCESSIBILITY
• TalkBack moves to the first setting when a page opens, and sliders announce their value once.
• TalkBack knows these voices work offline.

LOOK AND STABILITY
• A refreshed, modern design.
• Faster start-up and more reliable voice setup.
